column2: Ajahn Pasanno and Ajahn Jundee led a five-day retreat in Delhi in September 2018. There were fewer questions than usual.

column6: In the session we just had, you said that [if we] accept that the glass is meant to be broken, life is easier to handle. Isn't that a very pessimistic premise to begin with?

You mentioned a Zen teacher who said to make mistake after mistake until you finally find what you are looking for. In my experience when I move from one [spiritual] tradition to another, there's a sense of guilt---it's almost like cheating on the last tradition ... In my heart I know that it has served its purpose, but the guilt refuses to go.

I have a conflict between having a relationship and practicing Dhamma. I feel like it can't work together as my practice before my relationship. On one had I feel attached to her and the relationship, and on the other hand I feel attached to the path as I saw it before we met.
You mentioned that you were born as a Christian. Could you please share what brought you to Buddhism?

... Is the Middle Path a constant or variable? ... If I'm able to do more or less than another person, is my Middle Path different? ... I read that the Buddha always told monks to practice as much as possible. ... When there is a sense of urgency, does this break the Middle Path? ...
Ajahn Pasanno makes an adhiṭṭhāna for a Vassa not to make adhiṭṭhānas.
